product.amstrad-pc2386.summary: The PC2000 flagship targeted advanced work with a 32-bit architecture and cache memory.
product.amstrad-pc2386.history: Announced in September 1988, the PC2386 headed the PC2000 series for advanced workstation users, above the PC2286. The brochure offered a 65 MB disk, DOS 4.0 and Windows 386. The French price list dated 1 November 1988 set 34,190 francs excluding VAT for the HD 12 MD with a 12-inch monochrome monitor. The April 1989 brochure states assembly in Korea; Dataquest in September 1989 attributes manufacture to GPT in Kirkcaldy, Scotland. Both origins are documented, without identification by production batch.
product.amstrad-pc2386.warning: Historical card under research; it does not enable creation of a validated machine in BluMach.
product.amstrad-pc2386.technical.market: The series targeted professional users. Computerwoche reported its announcement on 30 September 1988; this does not establish the first sale date in each country.
product.amstrad-pc2386.technical.configu: A hard disk was part of the main offering. The brochure combines 65 MB with a high-density 3.5-inch floppy drive and four VGA monitor choices.
product.amstrad-pc2386.technical.memory: The cache reduced accesses to main memory. The brochure and manual document a 20 MHz 80386, 4 MB of parity RAM and 64 KB of 35 ns cache; the brochure advertises expansion to 16 MB on the motherboard. The optional 80387 coprocessor had a dedicated socket.
product.amstrad-pc2386.technical.video: The display did not require an additional card. The brochure documents integrated VGA and compatibility with EGA, CGA and Hercules.
product.amstrad-pc2386.technical.expansi: Sources disagree on the slot arrangement. The brochure, p. 7, and service manual, p. 2, specify five 16-bit slots; the brochure's back cover lists four 16-bit slots and one 8-bit slot. Both descriptions are shown.
product.amstrad-pc2386.technical.interfa: Printers and communications had dedicated connections. The documentation lists a bidirectional parallel port, RS-232 and a connector for external drives or tape.
product.amstrad-pc2386.technical.firmwar: The preserved dumps vary in quality. The set attributed to v1.11 contains four 32 KiB chips and allows a 64 KiB system image to be reconstructed. An older set has reset-vector problems and incomplete video data; different orderings and patches are not new original revisions.
product.amstrad-pc2386.technical.verifie: The archive supports study of the computer without certifying its emulation. The manual, dumps and reconstructions are preserved with hashes; BluMach 88f74ba3 does not register a dedicated pc2386 machine.
product.amstrad-pc2386.technical.limitat: Startup still needs to be demonstrated in BluMach. Firmware ordering and coverage must be confirmed and a dedicated model completed; results from other cores are not transferred. A publishable image awaits clear rights.
product.amstrad-pc2386.technical.brochur: Amstrad PC2000 Series, April 1989, pp. 3, 5 and 7 and back cover: configurations, hardware, assembly and two different slot descriptions.
product.amstrad-pc2386.technical.prices: Tarifs gamme PC2000, 1 November 1988: indicative French prices excluding VAT, with monitor and configuration specified.
product.amstrad-pc2386.technical.press: Computerwoche, Amstrad kommt mit PC-Serie 2000, 30 September 1988: announcement and each model's position.
product.amstrad-pc2386.technical.oem: Dataquest, Amstrad Plc, ESAM Volume I, September 1989, report 0004839, pp. 9–10: GPT in Kirkcaldy for PC2286/PC2386; this differs from Korean assembly stated in the brochure.
product.amstrad-pc2386.technical.manual: Amstrad PC2386 Service Manual, pp. 2, 19, 42 and 44: specifications, ROM and keyboard; a copy is preserved with its hash.
product.amstrad-pc2386.technical.firmwar: Internet Archive, PC 2386, v1.11: the description assigns 40189-2/40192-2 to IC156/IC159; the manual, p. 44, assigns 40189/40192 to IC159/IC156. Both references are retained; physical correspondence remains unresolved.
product.amstrad-pc2386.technical.source: BluMach source inspection at 88f74ba3: machine table and m_amstrad.c. This documents code presence, not verified operation.
product.amstrad-pc2386.technical.rom_ide: The sets archived under PC2286 and PC2386 share content. The four images 40189-2 through 40192-2 and the 64 KiB system reconstruction match byte for byte. This does not establish equivalent motherboards or validate compatibility.
